title: Launch Agent 7 separates ecosystem-wide from Agent-specific emergency response, and has written neither
content:
The Omni Documents reserve two separate emergency protocols. A.6.1.1.8.3.1.2 covers "situations that impact the entire Sky Ecosystem"; A.6.1.1.8.3.1.3 covers "situations solely impacting Launch Agent 7 versus the broader Sky Ecosystem." Both close with the identical sentence: "This protocol will be specified in a future iteration of the Launch Agent 7 Artifact."

The split itself is a design claim worth keeping even though the content is missing. Response is partitioned by blast radius, and that distinction has real consequences: an ecosystem-wide event calls for coordination with Sky and deference to ecosystem-level actors, while an Agent-only event calls for containment so the Agent's problem does not become Sky's. Collapsing the two would guarantee the wrong reflex in one of them.

The gap is the more pressing finding. Combined with the empty Non-Routine and Emergency protocols on the Ecosystem Upkeep primitives, Launch Agent 7 currently has exactly one specified emergency mechanism in the whole Artifact — the Operational Facilitator's power to accelerate a Root Edit (A.6.1.1.8.2.2.2.2.1.2.3.1).

That concentrates crisis response on a single lever, held by a role defined in another Agent's Artifact, whose transparency duty is explicitly waivable when disclosure would endanger the Agent. For an Agent running institutional credit facilities, the absence of both emergency protocols is a substantive rather than a cosmetic gap.
description: Two distinct protocols are reserved by blast radius — events hitting all of Sky versus only this Agent — with both deferred to future Artifact iterations.
